name: situ-activation
artifact_kind: freeze (pre-registration; written BEFORE any code, oracle or measurement)
base: origin/main 1e57b6d1 (the #439 / K3-REP-GATE-1 merge), semantics 19, K3 29/152 RED
claim: Kimi-K3's declared FFN combine — `hidden_act: "situ"` with `activation_situ_beta: 4.0` and `activation_situ_linear_beta: 25.0` — is DECLARED as a gate policy, CARRIED to the op plan, and EXECUTED on both the interpreter/CPU combine seam and the Metal lowering; and no execution path in this build can see a combine it cannot compute and silently compute plain gating instead.
non_claim: K3 does not execute. Its MLA layers still carry the q-LoRA triple, its latent-MoE wrapper is still unrepresented, its MXFP4 declaration is still unjudged, and its op plan still does not close. No witness here runs on a K3 container (none exists). Nothing is claimed about `topk_method`/`noaux_tc`, `moe_router_activation_func`, `latent_moe_use_norm`, `routed_expert_*`, `A_log [128]`, or the vision tower. No throughput, latency or quality claim of any kind. SiTU is not implemented on the walk / kquant / dense-weight paths — those REFUSE.

user_decisions_this_freeze_implements.scope_of_the_default_repair: FIX THE CLASS (the user, 2026-09-06). The defect is `a declared-but-unrecognised activation is treated identically to no activation declaration and silently becomes SiLU`, observed twice (K3 `situ`, BitNet `relu2`). The contract the user wrote out: checkpoint silent -> default permitted; declares a known thing -> execute it; declares an unknown thing -> REFUSE / report unknown; declares an unknown thing -> silently execute a default = NEVER.
user_decisions_this_freeze_implements.execution_depth: Combine seam AND a Metal kernel (the user's selection). Reconciled with the user's own prose constraint — `I would not turn K3-ACT-1 into a campaign to implement SiTU kernels in all 17 places` — as: ONE Metal kernel on the production lowered path (the direct sibling of the `clamped_glu_bias` kernel that already exists), and the 17 boolean-dispatch sites REFUSE BY NAME rather than gain implementations. This was stated back to the user before the freeze was written; if they meant the no-Metal option, the Metal arm is severable and the rest of this freeze stands unchanged.
user_decisions_this_freeze_implements.transitions: ONE. The user: `there isn't really an equivalent middle plane ... structurally it is an existing combine-policy mechanism receiving a new variant`. So declare + execute + refuse in a single transition, with no intermediate `unsupported_component` and therefore no RED -> AMBER flip.

D1_representation.decision: `ExpertGatePolicy::SituGlu { beta: f32, linear_beta: Option<f32> }` — a new arm on the existing policy enum. NOT an `Activation` variant.
D1_representation.authority: config/experts.rs L98-105, the enum's own doc, written about GPT-OSS and true word for word of SiTU: `Modelling that as "SiLU with extra steps" is how a forward pass ends up plausibly wrong — hence an explicit policy rather than an Activation variant.` An `Activation::Situ` would additionally have to carry two parameters through a table (`HF_ACTIVATION_NAMES`) whose rows are parameterless, and would land in 17 sites that reduce `Activation` to a bool.
D1_representation.linear_beta_is_Option_not_f32: the reference's `_get_situ_activation_params` returns `linear_beta` with NO fallback (L91), and L80 branches on `is not None`. Absent means the up branch is untouched — a different function, not `linear_beta = infinity`. `Option` is the type that says so.

D2_where_the_policy_is_resolved.decision: the `expert_gate_policy()` TRAIT DEFAULT (config/architecture.rs L1066), reading `hidden_act == "situ"` plus the two beta keys off `ModelConfig`. No architecture override.
D2_where_the_policy_is_resolved.why_this_does_not_contradict_the_standin: architecture.rs L1067-1082 refuses to derive the policy from `swiglu_limit` because `a declared parameter is not evidence of the operator that consumes it`. That reasoning is about a PARAMETER. `hidden_act` is the operator's NAME — the checkpoint's own module registers it as `ACT2FN["situ"] = SituAndMul` (modeling_kimi_linear.py L85), exactly the status `silu` and `gelu_pytorch_tanh` have, and exactly the status `swiglu`/`geglu` already have in `HF_GLU_NAMES` where a single word names a shape AND a nonlinearity. The comment is extended, not overruled, and the extension is written into it.
D2_where_the_policy_is_resolved.why_the_default_and_not_KimiLinearArch: `feedback_config_fact_belongs_in_trait_default`. The fact is a config fact, readable by any architecture; K3's text component is `kimi_linear`, shared with the 48B ancestor which declares `silu` — an override there would have to read `hidden_act` anyway, and would then be an architecture claiming to know better than a checkpoint that does not need correcting.

D3_the_activation_field_under_a_situ_pol.decision: `ExecutionSurface.ffn.activation` keeps holding an `Activation`, and under any non-`Gated` policy it is INERT BY CONSTRUCTION — `MoeGateRule::from_arch`'s match consumes `activation` only in the `Gated` arm, as it already does for `ClampedGlu`. A witness pins the inertness rather than asserting it: flipping the surface's activation from `Silu` to `GeluTanh` under a `SituGlu` policy must leave every combine output bit-identical.
D3_the_activation_field_under_a_situ_pol.the_probe_answers_from_the_combine_not_t: one new function, `larql_models::config::activation::hf_combine_name(policy, activation) -> Option<String>` — `SituGlu{..} => Some("situ")`, `Gated(a) => a.hf_name()`, `ClampedGlu{..} => None` (no HF word names it; GPT-OSS declares `silu` beside `swiglu_limit`, and returning `None` leaves that row on today's code path unchanged). `probe_activation` consults it. This is the decision that actually retires finding 44: without it the model would be correct and the plan would still read `mismatched`.
D3_the_activation_field_under_a_situ_pol.one_rule_owns_each_fact: carriage.rs L1316-1321 records why `hidden_act` was REMOVED from `canonical_declared` — normalising both sides made them disagree in opposite directions. `hf_combine_name` is added on the PROBE side only; `canonical_declared` is not touched.

D4_carriage_of_the_two_beta_keys.decision: two new `CarriageRule`s, `reaches: Carriage::Lowered`, site `ExecutionSurface.ffn.gate_policy (ExpertGatePolicy::SituGlu.beta / .linear_beta) -> FfnOp.gate_policy`, each with a probe that reads the value back off the built component's policy (the `probe_swiglu_limit` shape).
D4_carriage_of_the_two_beta_keys.why_Lowered_and_not_Represented: `swiglu_limit` claims `Represented` because the interpreter and the lowering both REFUSE a ClampedGlu FFN. Both execute SiTU after this rung, so `Lowered` is the congruent claim (`feedback_gate_claim_congruence`). `hidden_act` itself already claims `Lowered`; the parameters of the combine it names cannot honestly claim less.
D4_carriage_of_the_two_beta_keys.cluster: `SemanticCluster::FfnActivation` for both betas — the cluster `hidden_act` already carries (semantics.rs L997-1001). They are parameters of the activation the same cluster names; leaving them `Unclustered` would put a fact and its parameters in different clusters.

D5_the_beta_or_1_transcription.decision: normalised ONCE, at the point the policy is constructed (`expert_gate_policy()`'s default), and nowhere else. `beta` absent, null, or 0.0 -> 1.0; the reference's `beta or 1.0` (L91) is Python truthiness and 0.0 is falsy. `linear_beta` absent or null -> `None`; a declared 0.0 for `linear_beta` is NOT normalised (the reference has no `or` on it) and is carried verbatim — it makes the up branch identically zero, which is what the checkpoint would then be asking for.
D5_the_beta_or_1_transcription.witnessed: as its own test with all four inputs (absent, null, 0.0, 4.0), because a plausible implementation reads 0.0 literally and divides by zero, and no magnitude assertion elsewhere would catch it.

D6_the_seventeen_boolean_dispatch_sites.decision: REFUSE BY NAME. No SiTU implementation on the walk / kquant / dense-weight paths.
D6_the_seventeen_boolean_dispatch_sites.mechanism: one new trait method, `ModelArchitecture::gate_up_is_gelu_tanh(&self) -> bool`, which is the ONLY call those 17 sites make (each site changes from `arch.activation().uses_gelu_tanh_gate_up()` to `arch.gate_up_is_gelu_tanh()` — one token, no signature changes anywhere). Its default panics BY NAME when the declaration cannot be served there: a gate policy that is not plain gating (`SituGlu`, `ClampedGlu`), or an activation name this build has never judged (`relu2`).
D6_the_seventeen_boolean_dispatch_sites.why_a_panic_is_the_right_refusal_here: `Activation::uses_gelu_tanh_gate_up` ALREADY panics at this exact seam for `Activation::Relu`, with the message `has no gate/up FFN kernel on the walk/kquant paths (only gelu-tanh and SiLU are implemented)`. This extends an established contract rather than inventing one. These paths are reached only after a plan admits the model, and the plan refuses both specimens (K3 and BitNet are blocking today and stay blocking), so the panic is a backstop — which is what it should be. A `Result` here would change 17 signatures to defend against a state the planner already excludes.

D7_the_class_repair.decision: taken, in this rung, as the user directed.
D7_the_class_repair.what_changes: one new judgment function, `larql_models::config::activation::ActivationDeclaration::judge(hidden_act: Option<&str>)`, with four arms and NO fifth: `Absent` (the documented SiLU default, unchanged), `Nonlinearity(Activation)`, `NamesGatePolicy(&'static str)` (today: `situ` only), `Unjudged(String)` (today: `relu2` and anything else). `activation()`'s default is rewritten in terms of it, so `the config is silent` and `the config said something I cannot read` stop being the same branch — the divergence between that function's doc and its code (recon, `step_3_the_defect`) is closed by making the code match the doc.
D7_the_class_repair.where_the_refusal_actually_bites: `ActivationDeclaration::Unjudged` makes the executor refuse (D6's panic reads it), not the planner report differently. The planner ALREADY reports both specimens honestly — finding 44's `mismatched`/`execution_semantic`/blocking is the plan telling the truth. So the class repair's evidence is executor-side.
D7_the_class_repair.the_consequence_for_the_forecast_stated_: BitNet DOES NOT MOVE on the plan plane. `relu2` names no policy and no judged nonlinearity, so `hf_combine_name` never sees it, `probe_activation` behaves exactly as today, and its finding stays `mismatched`/`execution_semantic`/blocking with identical text. The 101-row activation blast radius the user accepted turns out to be SMALLER than feared: every plan-plane change is additive and reachable only under a `SituGlu` policy, which exactly one of the 117 rows declares. This is stated here, before measuring, so that a BitNet row that DOES move is a falsification of this freeze and not a discovery.

decisions_settled.D8_transitions: ONE. Declare + carry + execute + refuse, in one transition. No `unsupported_component` is introduced on `target.execution_surface`, so K3 does not flip RED -> AMBER (`feedback_verdict_moves_on_class_not_count`). K3 stays RED throughout, on a smaller number.

D9_oracle.decision: `scripts/situ_reference.py` (a verbatim transcription of `SituAndMul.forward`, L75-82, including the f32 upcast and the single final round) + `scripts/situ_oracle_export.py` -> `crates/larql-compute/src/ffn/expert_weight/tests/situ_oracle.json`, consumed by a parity test. Two ARMS, both legitimate configurations: `(beta = 4.0, linear_beta = 25.0)` = K3's, and `(beta = 4.0, linear_beta = None)` = the reference's own supported form.
D9_oracle.the_oracle_carries_its_own_controls: each control is exported as a named arm with its measured rel-L2 against the true arm, so a control that reads ~0 is visible in the fixture rather than absent from the test: `swiglu` (the actual defect on main), `gate_cap_omitted`, `up_cap_omitted`, `betas_swapped` (4.0 <-> 25.0), `sigmoid_omitted`, `tanh_omitted` (must agree with `swiglu` to within f32 — a check on the oracle itself), `cap_on_product`, `bf16_throughout` (measures whether L77-78's precision statement is observable; if it reads small it is RECORDED as small).
D9_oracle.the_saturation_gate: the fixture's (gate, up) band is ASSERTED to straddle the transition — at least one pair with |gate| < 1 (tanh nearly linear), one in 3..6, and one saturated — and the assertion is a test, not a comment. `feedback_saturated_softmax_blinds_an_oracle`: in the saturated regime SiTU degenerates to `+-beta * step(g) * u` and several controls above go numerically invisible. A control reading 0.0 because the fixture saturated is a blind instrument.
D9_oracle.why_not_the_hardcoded_style: `ffn/expert_weight/gate.rs::clamped_glu_matches_reference_implementation` hardcodes four PyTorch values. That is adequate for one arm and one control; it does not scale to two arms and eight controls, and it cannot assert a band. The hardcoded ClampedGlu test is NOT replaced.

decisions_settled.D10_semantics_version: PLANNER_SEMANTICS_VERSION 19 -> 20, with the identity pin's verdict pair extended: a synthetic estate declaring `situ` with both betas is admissible and executes; the same declaration on a path with no SiTU kernel is refused BY NAME; an estate declaring `relu2` is refused by name on the walk seam; the ancestor's `silu` estate is unchanged on every plane.

the three routed dispatch sites that match exhaustively on `MoeGateRule` — `moe_zero_copy.rs` L375, `moe_gpu_route/encode.rs` L245, `moe_dispatch/dispatch.rs` L256 — each gaining a `SituGlu` arm (they fail to compile until they do, which is the gate working)

the dense lowering: `lowering/ffn.rs`'s `FfnActivation` gains `SituGlu { beta, linear_beta }` (that enum is already lowering-local and documented as `the gate nonlinearity the lowering has a kernel for`, i.e. it is the lowering's combine rule, the same fold `MoeGateRule` performs), the one match at `encode_gate_up_act_from_normed` L279-283 gains an arm, and `vindex3_cmd/lowered/mod.rs`'s `ffn_activation` maps the policy
`lowered/mod.rs` L220-236's dense non-`Gated` refusal is narrowed to admit `SituGlu` and keep refusing `ClampedGlu` BY NAME

no performance claim, no bench, no shape sweep
D11_metal_scope.the_hazard_named_before_it_bites: the fused kernels above bake the activation INTO the gate/up dispatch. A plan that is admitted for the unfused path and then routed to a fused kernel would compute SwiGLU silently — the same defect one layer down. The refusal must be at the point the fused kernel is SELECTED, not only where the unfused one is encoded, and a witness must prove a SiTU plan cannot reach a fused arm.

falsification: Any of the following falsifies this freeze and is recorded as such rather than reinterpreted: K3 not landing exactly on 26; any finding added to the K3 row; any of P5-P8 moving by one byte; a control reading 0.0 without the fixture proving it could have read otherwise; a SiTU plan reaching a fused Metal kernel; or an execution entry point found after the fact that neither computes SiTU nor refuses by name. `feedback_unsatisfiable_gate_invites_reinterpretation`: none of these thresholds is adjusted after measurement.
